clusters.summary: Deleting the already-applied ConvertNegativeRatingToNull migration file makes Kysely's unconditional missing-migration check throw 'corrupted migrations' at startup for any database that recorded it, so those servers refuse to boot; keeping the file with a no-op up() avoids it.
clusters.rationale: runMigrations uses Kysely's Migrator with a FileMigrationProvider and rethrows any error; Kysely's migrator throws 'corrupted migrations: previously executed migration ... is missing' unconditionally when a recorded migration is absent from the folder, so any database that ran the now-deleted file (main/RC builds in the window since #27896) fails at startup. Confidence tempered because the population is pre-release only.

clusters.summary: Users who ran the deleted migration on main builds already had -1 ratings irreversibly converted to NULL, and the change ships no remediation or changelog note acknowledging it.
clusters.rationale: True that main-branch databases which ran the migration in the ~3-day window (v3.0.0 unreleased; last tag v2.7.5) had -1 set to NULL irreversibly, but no remediation is possible and the affected population is pre-release; the actionable part of the migration-deletion concern is g22.

clusters.summary: Metadata extraction still clamps with validateRange(exifTags.Rating, 1, 5), so a -1 rating (whether set via the API and written to the sidecar, or authored externally as XMP 'rejected') is converted to NULL on the next extraction, silently losing the rejection.
clusters.rationale: metadata extraction still uses validateRange(exifTags.Rating, 1, 5), which returns null for -1, while handleSidecarWrite writes Rating -1 to the sidecar and then unlocks the property; so a -1 set via the API (or authored externally as XMP rejected) is silently dropped to NULL on the next extraction. #27896 changed this from (-1, 5) and this PR does not revert it.

clusters.summary: BaseSearchSchema.rating still carries .min(1) (and the '-1 no longer valid' history entry), so every derived search DTO rejects rating -1 with HTTP 400 and rejected assets can be set but never searched for, while the search and asset DTO histories now contradict each other.
clusters.rationale: BaseSearchSchema.rating still has .min(1).max(5) and the 'v3: Using -1 as a rating is no longer valid' history entry, so all derived search DTOs return 400 for rating -1 after this PR makes -1 settable, and the search and asset histories now contradict each other. Incomplete revert of #27896, not raised by any thread.

clusters.summary: Moving the rating bounds from .min()/.max() into a .refine() hides them from the JSON-Schema emitter, so UpdateAssetDto/AssetBulkUpdateDto.rating publish minimum/maximum ±9007199254740991 in the OpenAPI spec and generated Dart client instead of a bounded range.
clusters.rationale: Moving the bounds into .refine() leaves z.int()'s safe-integer bag min/max as the only emitted bounds, so the spec and generated clients publish minimum -9007199254740991 / maximum 9007199254740991 for the rating field; this is exactly thread 1's 'wrong/misleading' comment on that spec line.

clusters.summary: ExifResponseDto.rating still declares z.int().min(1).max(5) while GET /assets/:id can now return exifInfo.rating -1, so the response contract contradicts actual values (no runtime failure today only because no @ZodSerializerDto is applied).
clusters.rationale: ExifResponseSchema.rating is still z.int().min(1).max(5) (added by #27896) so the published response contract says 1..5 while the server can now return -1; no runtime failure because no controller uses ZodSerializerDto, but the spec is wrong for consumers.

clusters.summary: The web UI passes a -1 rating through `asset.exifInfo?.rating || null` cast as Rating (1-5|null), so a rejected asset renders with no stars filled and is indistinguishable from unrated (pre-existing behavior made reachable again).
clusters.rationale: -1 is truthy so it is passed as Rating and StarRating fills no stars ((-1||0) >= value is false), so a rejected asset looks unrated apart from the 'clear' button; a real, pre-existing web gap the server-only PR re-exposes, but out of the PR's scope and longstanding.

clusters.summary: The duplicate-keeper tie-break heuristic counts truthy exif values, so a -1 rating counts as 'has a rating' and nudges a rejected asset ahead where null would not (pre-existing).
clusters.rationale: True that -1 is truthy and counts toward the EXIF tie-break, but a rejected asset does carry rating information, and this only nudges a size tie-break; pre-existing and not worth reviewer attention.

clusters.summary: Duplicate merge only propagates a rating when rating > 0, so merging a rejected (-1) duplicate into an unrated keeper silently drops the rejection and trashes the duplicate (pre-existing, made reachable again).
clusters.rationale: The merge loop takes the max rating starting from 0 and only writes it when > 0, so a -1 duplicate merged into an unrated keeper leaves the keeper unrated; correct trace of pre-existing behavior that -1 makes reachable again, but whether a rejection should propagate to the keeper is debatable, so it is small.

clusters.summary: The new v3 x-immich-history text 'Using 0 as a rating is no longer valid' on the asset rating field was questioned for accuracy/completeness — it is factually correct (0 was previously coerced to null) but says nothing about -1 being valid again.
clusters.rationale: A considered-and-cleared note: the 'Using 0 as a rating is no longer valid' entry is accurate (0 was previously coerced to null by a transform, now rejected by the refine); the residual point that the history does not mention -1 being re-allowed is a wording preference already covered by g01.

clusters.summary: The change deletes the shipped v2.6.0 '-1 deprecated' x-immich-history entry instead of superseding it with a v3 entry stating -1 is valid again, rewriting a published API changelog that reads as append-only and leaving asset.dto.ts and search.dto.ts disagreeing about v2.6.0.
clusters.rationale: The v2.6.0 deprecation entry that shipped in a release is deleted from asset.dto.ts's history rather than superseded, while search.dto.ts still carries both the v2.6.0 and 'v3: -1 no longer valid' entries, so the two published histories now contradict each other. Real but small; the substantive half (search still rejecting -1) is g14.

clusters.summary: Rating 0 now returns 400 instead of being coerced to null as before the original restriction — a distinct breaking change that no commit message mentions and no test pins.
clusters.rationale: At the diff's base commit rating 0 was already rejected by .min(1) (introduced by #27896, marked refactor!), so this PR does not introduce the 0->400 change; and the diff itself documents it via the new 'v3: Using 0 as a rating is no longer valid' history entry. Only the 'no test pins 0' kernel is true, and it is minor.

clusters.summary: The .int().nullable().refine(...).optional() chain ordering on rating was probed for mis-handling omitted/null values and found behaviorally equivalent to the old .nullish() (no defect).
clusters.rationale: Considered-and-cleared: .nullable() then .refine() accepting null then .optional() behaves the same as .nullish() for omitted/null values; asserts no defect.

clusters.summary: The refine predicate was suspected of double-reporting on non-integers; 3.5 emits only the int error, though 1e21 emits two issues with no covering test.
clusters.rationale: Mostly a cleared suspicion: 3.5 yields only the int error (invalid_type is aborting, continue:false), and an unsafe integer like 1e21 yields a non-aborting too_big plus the refine message; two error strings on a nonsense input is cosmetic and not worth reviewer attention.

clusters.summary: The refine error message 'Must be -1, a number from 1 to 5, or null' mixes a literal, a range, and nullability and reads oddly against surrounding message style.
clusters.rationale: Stylistic preference about the refine error string; the message is accurate and unambiguous. Not the same substance as thread 2, which is about the .describe() text.

clusters.summary: Rating field descriptions have drifted across asset.dto.ts, search.dto.ts, and exif.dto.ts, and the new user-facing 'rejected' concept is documented nowhere including the XMP sidecar docs.
clusters.rationale: The three rating field descriptions now disagree ('-1 (rejected)' vs '[1-5], or null' vs 'Rating') and the rejected semantics are documented nowhere; true and actionable but small, and the search half largely follows from g14.

clusters.summary: Commit messages contain typos ('udpate tests', 'gen clientc') and should be squashed before merge.
clusters.rationale: Commit-message typos on a PR that will be squash-merged; not a code concern.

clusters.summary: SearchRatingsSection's Number.parseInt on the 'null' option yields NaN and options[rating] indexing is off by one for ratings 1-5 (pre-existing, unrelated to -1).
clusters.rationale: options[0] is the 'null' entry and options[1..5] are ratings 1..5, so options[rating] is not off by one; Number.parseInt('null') is NaN but serializes to JSON null, which is what the search API expects for unrated. Also pre-existing and unrelated to the diff by its own admission.

clusters.summary: Whether the object-level lat/long .refine() on UpdateAssetBaseSchema survives .extend() in Zod v4 is worth confirming, though the pattern is untouched by this diff.
clusters.rationale: Zod 4's util.extend keeps the object's checks (it only throws when the new shape overwrites an existing key), and the refine/extend pattern is untouched by the diff and exercised by the existing lat/long tests; a 'worth confirming' note with no defect.

clusters.summary: media.repository.ts's Rating mapping (null -> 0, else pass-through) was traced and a -1 rating passes through unchanged — no defect.
clusters.rationale: Considered-and-cleared: `Rating: tags.rating === null ? 0 : tags.rating` passes -1 through; asserts no defect.

clusters.summary: The generated mobile Dart models appearing as binary diffs is a diff-tool artifact for generated files, not a content defect.
clusters.rationale: Explains a diff-rendering artifact for generated files; no defect asserted.

clusters.summary: No test asserts that rating -1 is accepted: the controller spec's as-is loop still covers only 1 and 5, and the negative-rating e2e, unit (metadata.service.spec), and round-trip coverage deleted by the original restriction is not restored, so a regression re-restricting -1 would pass CI.
clusters.rationale: The as-is loop still tests only ratings 1 and 5, and the negative-rating e2e and metadata.service.spec cases removed by #27896 are not restored, so nothing in CI asserts -1 is accepted; correct and actionable, small to fix.

clusters.summary: The earlier ConvertRating0ToNull migration is untouched by this diff and not implicated in the migration deletion.
clusters.rationale: Notes an unrelated file is untouched; asserts no defect.

clusters.summary: The controller spec's over-max (7) and under-min (-2) rejection cases now assert the same error string, losing diagnostic granularity between the two boundaries (still not a vacuous pass).
clusters.rationale: Both boundary cases now assert the same refine message, an inherent consequence of a single refine; the test still fails on a wrong status or message, so this is a preference, not a defect.

clusters.summary: Pre-existing rating consumers for sorting and workflow execution were checked and are untouched, with no -1 interaction found.
clusters.rationale: Considered-and-cleared note that other rating consumers are unaffected; asserts no defect.

clusters.summary: The mobile rating_bar widget was checked for a crash on rating -1; it renders all stars unfilled with no assert, so the scenario dissolved.
clusters.rationale: Considered-and-cleared: `_currentRating > index` with -1 renders no filled stars and there is no assert; asserts no defect.

clusters.summary: The generated Dart client was checked for rejecting rating -1 by range; update_asset_dto.dart does a bare int.parse with no bounds enforcement, so construction cannot fail.
clusters.rationale: Considered-and-cleared: the generated Dart model does no range enforcement; asserts no defect.

clusters.summary: The oasdiff breaking-change gate was considered; relaxing minimum/maximum on a request property widens what is accepted and is not breaking, so the check stays green.
clusters.rationale: Considered-and-cleared: widening request-property bounds is not a breaking change for oasdiff's fail-on ERR gate; asserts no defect.
